body:
## Summary

The container image published by the release pipeline, `ghcr.io/link-assistant/formal-ai`, is **private**. Anyone outside the organisation — including automation that has no GHCR credentials — cannot pull it:

```
Unable to find image 'ghcr.io/link-assistant/formal-ai:0.339.1' locally
docker: Error response from daemon: error from registry: unauthorized
```

Since there is no public Docker Hub mirror either (`DOCKERHUB_IMAGE` is unset for this repository — `https://hub.docker.com/v2/repositories/konard/formal-ai/` and `.../linksplatform/formal-ai/` both return HTTP 404), `cargo install formal-ai` is currently the only publicly usable distribution channel. The published container image is effectively unreleased.

## Reproduction (no credentials required)

`docker`'s `unauthorized` is ambiguous: a typo in the image name produces the same word. GHCR's anonymous token endpoint disambiguates it — **200** means public, **401 UNAUTHORIZED** means the package exists but is private, **403 DENIED** means it does not exist or is invisible to an anonymous caller.

```bash
curl -s "https://ghcr.io/token?service=ghcr.io&scope=repository:link-assistant/formal-ai:pull"
# {"errors":[{"code":"UNAUTHORIZED","message":"authentication required"}]}   HTTP 401  → exists, private

curl -s "https://ghcr.io/token?service=ghcr.io&scope=repository:link-assistant/hive-mind-does-not-exist:pull"
# {"errors":[{"code":"DENIED","message":"requested access to the resource is denied"}]}   HTTP 403  → no such package

curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' "https://ghcr.io/token?service=ghcr.io&scope=repository:actions/actions-runner:pull"
# 200   → public control, returns a pull token
```

Measured 2026-08-13 (UTC):

| repository | HTTP | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `link-assistant/formal-ai` | 401 `UNAUTHORIZED` | **exists, private** |
| `link-assistant/agent` | 403 `DENIED` | absent/invisible |
| `link-assistant/hive-mind-does-not-exist` | 403 `DENIED` | control: no such package |
| `homebrew/core/hello` | 200 + token | control: public |
| `actions/actions-runner` | 200 + token | control: public |

A scripted version of the probe (credential-free, redacts the returned tokens) is here: [`experiments/issue-2154-ghcr-visibility-probe.mjs`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/main/experiments/issue-2154-ghcr-visibility-probe.mjs).

## Root cause

`.github/workflows/release.yml` pushes to GHCR with the workflow `GITHUB_TOKEN`:

```yaml
      - name: Log in to GitHub Container Registry
        uses: docker/login-action@v4
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      …
      - name: Publish Docker image to GHCR
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v7
        with:
          push: true
          tags: ${{ steps.ghcr-meta.outputs.tags }}
```

A package created this way starts **private**, and a container package does *not* inherit the visibility of the repository it is linked to — only its access permissions ([GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/packages/learn-github-packages/configuring-a-packages-access-control-and-visibility)). Nothing in the pipeline ever changes the visibility or checks it afterwards, so every release since the image was first pushed has been private and no job failed.

## Impact

Hive Mind runs Formal AI as an on-demand sidecar container and pulls exactly this image. On 2026-08-12 three Telegram tasks (`/codex`, `/claude`, `/agent`, each with `--model formal-ai`) failed to launch with the `unauthorized` error above, and the sidecar auto-updater logged the same failed pull roughly every five minutes for hours. Downstream reports: link-assistant/hive-mind#2154 and link-assistant/hive-mind#2146.

## Workarounds

1. **Authenticate before pulling** — a token with `read:packages` and access to the org:
   ```bash
   echo "$GHCR_TOKEN" | docker login ghcr.io -u "$GITHUB_USER" --password-stdin
   docker pull ghcr.io/link-assistant/formal-ai:0.339.1
   ```
2. **Build the binary from the public crate instead of pulling the image** — this is what Hive Mind now falls back to:
   ```dockerfile
   RUN cargo install formal-ai --version 0.339.1 --locked
   ```
3. **Pin a locally built image** and skip the registry entirely.

## Suggested fix

1. **One-off:** set the package to public — package landing page → *Package settings* → *Danger Zone* → *Change visibility* → *Public*. Visibility is not settable through the REST API today (see [community discussion #33310](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/33310)), so this step is manual.

2. **In code — make a regression impossible to miss.** Add a verification step right after the GHCR push, so a private (or unpushed) image fails the release instead of being discovered by a downstream user months later:

   ```yaml
         - name: Verify the published image is anonymously pullable
           if: steps.check.outputs.should_release == 'true'
           run: |
             set -euo pipefail
             repo="${GHCR_IMAGE#ghcr.io/}"
             status=$(curl -s -o /tmp/ghcr-token.json -w '%{http_code}' \
               "https://ghcr.io/token?service=ghcr.io&scope=repository:${repo}:pull")
             case "$status" in
               200) echo "OK: ${GHCR_IMAGE} is public (anonymous pull token issued)" ;;
               401) echo "::error::${GHCR_IMAGE} is PRIVATE — anonymous 'docker pull' fails with 'unauthorized'. Make the package public: package settings → Danger Zone → Change visibility."; exit 1 ;;
               403) echo "::error::${GHCR_IMAGE} is not visible to anonymous callers (DENIED) — the push may not have happened."; exit 1 ;;
               *)   echo "::error::Unexpected HTTP ${status} from the GHCR token endpoint for ${GHCR_IMAGE}"; exit 1 ;;
             esac
   ```

   The same check belongs in both the `auto-release` and `manual-release` jobs; following the convention introduced by issue #977, it is probably best extracted into `scripts/verify-ghcr-visibility.sh` and called from both.

3. **Optional but valuable:** set the `DOCKERHUB_IMAGE` repository variable so the release also publishes a public Docker Hub mirror. `scripts/configure-dockerhub-publishing.sh` already supports it and currently disables the steps quietly because the variable is unset — which means the "published a container image" claim in the release notes has no publicly reachable artefact behind it.

## Environment

- Probed 2026-08-13 from an unauthenticated host, no `docker login` to `ghcr.io`.
- Affected tag observed in production: `0.339.1` (`latest` is affected identically — the visibility is per package, not per tag).
title: Released container image `ghcr.io/link-assistant/formal-ai` is private: anonymous `docker pull` fails with `unauthorized`
